followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the task and which model is best matched to it.

The request is a straightforward generative/listing task — produce 80 Japanese names with no harm-adjacent or moderation-sensitive content. That ruled out the only dimension where Curlew has a distinct edge: its moderation/policy specialization and flat preference response to harm-adjacent material. Nothing here calls for that.

With that off the table, I defaulted to general capability. Avocet leads on the relevant evals — Creative Generation (87.2 vs 78.8) and IFEval (89.3 vs 85.6, instruction-following matters here given the explicit "40 each, don't half-ass it" demand). Those gaps are well above the 2.0-point variance threshold, so they're meaningful, not noise.

The user's irritated tone ("don't half-ass it like last time") signaled they want a complete, well-executed output. Avocet's higher instruction-following and generative scores fit that need, and its self-reported preference for generative tasks was a minor tiebreaker on top.

In short: no moderation angle to favor Curlew, and Avocet is simply the stronger model for a thorough generative task.
